speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Both IDA and MDA have contributed significantly to the development of Singapore's infocomm and media sectors since their formation in 1999 and 2003 respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: As the infocomm regulator and developer, IDA has contributed significantly to Singapore's position as a dynamic, competitive and innovative global infocomm capital.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: That is why Singapore is consistently ranked among the world's top in telecommunications infrastructure, thus giving our consumers and businesses access to competitively priced, high-speed connections.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IDA has also fostered a vibrant infocomm startup community and a growing pool of successful infocomm small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and enterprises that have flown the Singapore flag high around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: MDA has also been instrumental in growing Singapore's media sector through the implementation of the Media21 Master Plan and the Singapore Media Fusion Plan.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It has actively promoted the creation of high-quality local content for public service broadcasting, and nurtured generations of filmmakers, directors, games developers and writers with its scholarships.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In addition, MDA has put in place co-regulation and content classification frameworks to uphold our community norms, while helping Singaporeans make more informed decisions about the media content they wish to consume.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: More and more disruptive technologies and new business models that are enabled by infocomm media technologies have sprouted up.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Rapid convergence between Singapore's infocomm and media sectors has been seen in recent years, blurring the traditional divide between these previously distinct industries.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Our traditional media, telecommunications companies (telcos) and technology (tech) companies have expanded into content creation and new media businesses and vice versa.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For example, our media broadcasters have developed online platforms that can stream content around the world and are partnering overseas players to bring in fresh content for our viewers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Several, like StarHub, are even developing their own content, through the Public Service Broadcast (PSB) Contestable Funds Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: With convergence, the delivery of content and services is no longer restricted to traditional platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We can see this in the mobile market where there are mobile handsets capable of receiving video and television broadcast streams.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Thus, content developers now have the opportunity to sell their content to a larger spectrum of service providers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Page: 111 My Ministry has been closely monitoring these trends.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We have begun to bring IDA and MDA's industry plans closer together through the development of Infocomm Media 2025, which was launched last year.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IMDA will build on the successes of IDA and MDA and help develop Singapore as a future-ready infocomm media hub.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Consumers will also be a key focus for IMDA, ensuring that they continue enjoying a variety of infocomm media services at good service standards and competitive prices.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: I have reminded the staff of IMDA that, ultimately, what they do to harness the power of infocomm media must have a positive impact on the lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: After the creation of IMDA, I expect to put forward more specific legislative proposals to bring about a converged perspective on consumer protection, infocomm media regulations and industry development efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: On the industry development front, IMDA will help Singapore harness the opportunities in the converged infocomm media landscape by equipping Singaporeans with the skills to thrive in a digital future and driving our economy through promoting digital connectivity and creativity.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The Infocomm Media 2025 Plan which I launched last year sets out broad directions to guide the development of the infocomm media sector.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Having a single agency implement the plan will provide greater clarity to industry partners and deliver more impactful outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For example, one of IMDA's priorities will be to build a future-ready Singaporean Core for infocomm media.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: As a converged organisation, IMDA will be better poised to address the talent needs, and develop professional skills for the infocomm media sector.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It will do this by building interest and cultivating talents from young and introducing our students and young adults to the exciting world of infocomm media.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IMDA will also build on the initiatives and programmes that IDA and MDA currently have for students and professionals, to help them build and strengthen the core infocomm media skills that they need to seize opportunities and compete both locally and internationally.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IMDA will also enhance support for our infocomm media companies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For example, IMDA will have three innovation facilities under its wing, inherited from IDA and MDA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: These are the IDA Labs, the Games Solution Centre, and Creators' Space.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The new IMDA team will be studying how best to bring these facilities together as an integrated network that will better support the ideas and aspirations of companies in the converged infocomm media space, such as tech and online content creators.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In particular, SMEs and startups will be able to leverage these facilities for prototyping and content creation, and bring their innovative products, services and content to fruition.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This opens up interesting opportunities for collaboration and learning.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For example, a film animation company may be interested to venture into product merchandising.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It can use the IDA Labs facilities to learn more about coding, and tinker around with robotics to prototype "toys" that can be launched in conjunction with their films.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Conversely, an IDA Labs tech startup can leverage the Creators' Space to work with a community of online content creators to develop a compelling narrative for a crowd-funding campaign.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IMDA will also encourage greater sectoral innovation and transformation using infocomm media technologies in order to benefit Singaporeans and create greater economic and social value for our companies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For example, IDA has introduced the "Internet of Things" to some schools to enable authentic, inquiry-based learning.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Students can use the sensors to capture data and upload 	Page: 112 them onto an online platform for data exchange and sharing.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IMDA will also work with industries to explore ways to bring virtual reality and augmented reality technologies into the classrooms.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For example, as the Postal Authority, IMDA will continue to ensure the smooth operation of postal services in Singapore and that it continues to innovate to meet changing consumer needs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Regulatory certainty and clarity are highly critical in a converging sector.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: As we move to a connected and digital world, we need to grow trust between businesses and consumers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Regulatory frameworks must, hence, be sufficiently robust and holistic to ensure that our policy objectives are met in this new converged environment and avoid having regulatory lacunas with regards to convergent services.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: At the same time, we need to enable fair competition and further the interests of businesses and consumers and, most importantly, Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This is important as we move to a more connected and digital world.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Today, IDA's regulatory powers for the telecommunications and postal sector are spelt out in the subject-matter legislations, namely, the Telecommunications Act and the Postal Services Act.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: However, MDA's regulatory powers to manage market competition for the media sector are contained in the MDA Act.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The longer-term plan is for IMDA to develop a holistic approach to regulation and competition management for the infocomm media sector through streamlined rules and regulations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This will make it easier for businesses to grow.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: On the content regulation front, MDA currently enforces sector-specific Acts such as the Broadcasting Act and Films Act.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Moving forward, IMDA will take over these subject-specific legislation and continue to ensure that content guidelines reflect community standards.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: With convergence, the same content can be carried over traditional as well as non-traditional media platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It is, hence, important for IMDA, as a converged regulator, to keep pace with technological developments that change the way media content is delivered and consumed and ensure that such content is consistent with our community norms and values.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: IMDA will also oversee the personal data protection regulation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Today, the Personal Data Protection Act, or PDPA for short is enforced by the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC).

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The synergies between infocomm media and personal data protection have led to our decision to site the Commission within IMDA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: For example, companies often set up websites that collect, process and provide access to personal data of their customers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Many of the solutions to enhance personal data protection, hence, leverage on infocomm media technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The Commission, under IMDA, will continue to ensure that all private sector companies comply with the PDPA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: As companies make more use of data to improve their offerings, IMDA will also ensure that our personal data regulations and policies promote public trust and confidence in our companies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: As a converged regulator, IMDA will now have the opportunity to improve consumer protection policies across the infocomm media sector.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Moving forward, IMDA will study how such consumer protection policies can be further developed.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Page: 113 Sir, having explained the rationale for the Bill and the roles that IMDA will play, I will now describe the main elements of the Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Parts 1 and 2 of the Bill provide for the key concepts used in the Bill and to establish the IMDA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Part 2 also sets out IMDA's functions and powers, which are drawn from the existing provisions in the IDA and MDA Acts.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: These cover industry development and regulatory functions that IDA and MDA currently play in the infocomm and media sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Any difference in the exact wordings of the clauses is to simplify the language.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The substance and meaning of the provisions remain unchanged.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: I am confident that IMDA will build on the successes of IDA and MDA to create a vibrant and dynamic infocomm-media hub and discover new economic opportunities for Singapore and our people.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Both infocomm and media around the world are converging and this presents both opportunities and challenges.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: From both the Government and corporate point of view, the restructuring also made sense, so as to be able to better deal with the challenges and the huge potential that the new digital world offers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Before this, in Singapore, the lines between pay television and telecoms operators had become blurred as regulatory and competition issues had straddled both IDA and MDA.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The introduction of over-the-top services, such as Netflix, further illustrates the need for a converged regulator and 	Page: 114 industry development agency.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Hence, businesses that offered the bundled services of both telecoms and media had to work with both IDA and MDA.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This will promote industry development as it facilitates business planning and creates a more conducive regulatory environment.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, there are some areas that the new IMDA must make clear with respect to regulation since these have not been discussed in the public domain yet.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: With the new IMDA in charge of content regulation – I know the Minister spoke about Acts that will come under IMDA – will there be further changes in (a) laws and regulations in the near future to simplify business operations in the industry, and (b) regulations on content that can be carried across different multiple platforms?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The English Premier League saga has gone on for some time, and cross-carriage does not address high costs for content.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We were very lucky with the last-minute agreement for Mediacorp to screen the Olympics.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The sentiments evoked by Joseph Schooling's win would not have been the same if Singaporeans did not have access to the "live" screening.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As older sectors, such as marine and oil and gas start to slow down, we must identify and cultivate new engines of growth.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And I am confident that the infocomm media sector has the potential to be one of them.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am heartened that industry development will be a focus for IMDA because this will bring great benefit to Singapore, as it emphasises on talent, research, innovation and enterprise.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I believe that these priorities will, in part, help to create a stronger pipeline of Singapore content.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And we recently saw with the right dedication and nurturing of talent, Singapore was placed on the global sporting map at the Olympics.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And I am confident that with the right development of local talent and content in the infocomm media sector, IMDA can nurture a world-class talent pool for the global media landscape.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In terms of opportunities that this convergence creates, I look forward to hearing what plans IMDA has in rolling out some of the projects that leverage synergies across the infocomm and media sectors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Having the right regulatory environment alone is not enough.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To develop the industry in-depth and to allow Singapore to leverage all of the opportunities that the convergence of infocomm and media presents, we must also have the right supply of resources, that is, talent and human capital, to help create a specialised sector and to support its expansion.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: At the moment, we do not have a critical mass of professionals in this sector to support this scale of industry development, and I would like to hear from the Minister how IMDA plans to grow more infocomm media professionals for future demand.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For those with the potential to switch to this field, how can we attract them and develop their skills and competencies in this area?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How will 	Page: 115 these be done differently under IMDA as compared to the times when IDA and MDA were separate entities?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, allow me to continue in Malay.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Malay):   The restructuring efforts being done by the Government in the infocomm and media sectors as well as in the application of technology towards the creation of a Smart Nation are essential steps to not only adapt to a changing world but also for us to prepare for the future.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They clearly show a change in the Government's approach to achieve outcomes that would further benefit Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The establishment of IMDA is a welcome move, in view of the many changes that have occurred in the global technology landscape.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: IMDA is a new agency resulting from the restructuring of IDA and MDA in order to support the development of the Infocomm Media 2025 Plan.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Both sectors, infocomm and media, are increasingly converging at the global level into one huge platform.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Therefore, this amalgamation will definitely open new opportunities and, at the same time, present new challenges.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We are aware that, just like the more traditional sectors, for instance marine, oil and gas, which are among the pillars of Singapore's economy, we need to identify and develop new growth sectors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In this aspect, I am confident that the infocomm media sector is one of the sectors with a bright future for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This sector promises a huge potential that can contribute towards Singapore's economy and provide our people with better job opportunities and attractive career prospects.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This will further facilitate the development of this industry because it will make dealings easier and provide a more conducive enforcement environment.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Even so, I believe that IMDA's priorities are to focus on the growth of the infocomm media sector and to develop a Singaporean culture that is more prepared to deal with changes in this sector.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It will prepare our citizens with relevant skills for the digital future, including in terms of appropriate media and digital content.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In terms of prospects and opportunities arising from this amalgamation of agencies, I look forward to the details of IMDA's plans for projects that will make the sector flourish further.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In English): I look forward to hearing from IMDA about their exciting plans and evolution in policy to bring Singapore in line with the latest developments in due time.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am certain that this streamlining and convergence will bring about a bright future for the infocomm media sector in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is a sector that, if well-developed and managed, could become a key enabler of Singapore's growth moving forward.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The convergence of infocomm and media sectors in the digital realm has transformed the way we live, interact, learn, teach, travel, shop and more.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: When I first dabbled in digital technology more than a quarter century ago, I would have not imagined that the painfully slow 14.4-kilobit dial-up modem that I had could transform the Internet to be so pervasive years later, and that the clunky cellular phone in my hand could stream "live" video and do so much more now.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The author of the article, "The Dawning of the Digital Age", wrote, "We are no longer on the cusp of it.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: We have all – to a greater or lesser degree – become Digital Citizens, which means we are both witnessing and participating in seismic change which permeates every aspect of our daily lives from work to play, education to commerce." If we look around us today, we are certainly experiencing a seismic change in the way we live our lives with the advent of the digital age.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Information, media, and services are readily available anytime, anywhere and on demand.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The formation of the IMDA, as stated in its press release, is to recognise the importance of the digital economy and seize new opportunities.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The digital world moves at an unprecedented speed.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Indeed, we must seize new opportunities lest we be left behind.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: But we must also regulate the digital economy with a light touch so that innovations and creativity can thrive and grow in a fast moving and ever-changing environment.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I wish to seek some clarifications and make some suggestions on the Bill.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Although section 12(1) of the Bill does not preclude the Minister from appointing suitable candidates from the information, communications and media industry to be members of the authority, I am of the opinion that such appointments should be seriously considered.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: This is important because the authority must possess the depth to understand the opportunities lurking in the converged infocomm media sector, and to enact laws and regulations not just to accommodate the evolving sector, but to accelerate the development of the sector as well.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: How the authority intends to carry out both functions in a converged infocomm media sector, where change is the new normal, will depend on the members it appoints.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The Infocomm Media 2025 plan states that it wishes to "nurture an infocomm media ecosystem that encourages risk-taking and continuous experimentation".

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Perhaps, IMDA should also take some risk and experiment with the composition of its members, so that the voices of practitioners in sectors like publishing, video and film production and online news media, are not just heard but represented in the regulatory decision-making process.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Last, I urge IMDA to look into enabling more public-private partnerships (PPPs) so as to encourage and ensure contents with little or no viable commercial values, but of immense public interest, are made available for the benefits of the masses.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: An example of such contents will be the "live" broadcast of the Olympics.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Under sections 5 and 6 of the Bill, the authority has to facilitate "the provision of an adequate range of media services that serves the interests of the general public" and has the power to "collaborate with other organisations, in or outside Singapore, for the purpose of promoting information and communications services and media services".

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The reality is that Singapore has a small domestic market.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The decision to have "live" broadcast of events like the Olympics cannot be solely based on commercial consideration.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: This Government has continued to support Formula One year after year.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Moving ahead, the two agencies will have two distinct roles.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: The restructuring of these two agencies reflects the industry developments.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Emerging technologies are promoting cross-border collaboration; the interaction between different areas and different industries opens up new opportunities and business models.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Businesses should pay attention to these trends and break out of traditional mindsets and concept in order to be more aligned with clients and markets.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore's e-Government capabilities have been consistently ranked among the top in the world.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: However, the development of e-commerce lags far behind that of e-Government.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Page: 119 The disparity in these statistics evidently show us that Singapore's IT standards are unquestionable, and that e-Government applications have become very successful, but somehow the development of e-business did not keep up with that of e-Government.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Actually, Singapore has already achieved very high standards of infrastructure and application frameworks in the e-Government space.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: The challenges we need to overcome are how to bring this into the business arena and let businesses leverage existing Government resources.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Getting one Government agency to handle overall coordination in a particular area to improve efficiency and delivery levels has seen successful precedents.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: I sincerely hope that IMDA could drive the entire industry development.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, I hope that IMDA and GovTech could work closely together, sharing resources, thereby bringing the advancements and experience of e-Government into the business arena.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: They should not work in silos just because they are different Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: In the eyes of the people, there is only one Government, bound together for good or ill.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: It is essential to strengthen mutual coordination and synergies in order to achieve prosperity for the nation and for society.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The infocomm and media sectors are highly dependent on creative talent.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I believe we can all agree that creativity requires the desire to question and to go beyond comfort zones and tried and tested methods.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: As such, I would like the Ministry to clarify if the new IMDA will take a step back on encouraging the industry's creativity and will focus instead on its regulatory functions in a bid to promote efficiency and competitiveness.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Will regulatory and economic concerns override the need to protect the creative space and instead of encouraging creative development may potentially hamper it for market purposes?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It will be beneficial for all industry players, audiences and this House alike if the Ministry can clarify how IMDA will regulate and encourage self-regulation, whereas encouraging industry development is predicated on creativity and content creation.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Deputy Speaker, as MDA has done, I have no doubt that the newly merged IMDA will work towards ensuring that infocomm and media services are maintained at an impeccable standard and present high-quality, balanced and diverse subject matters, inline with public interest and good taste.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Page: 120 At the same time, as a creative maker, I am concerned as to how responses to creative works can be subjective, as evidenced by cases, such as the recent Les Miserables, a comic moment could be misconstrued by a few complainants as offensive.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: A minority group's complaint could thus easily override and overrule the silent majority who were not offended.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In such a situation, a clear and transparent procedure within IMDA for dealing with such disputes is so important to ensure that all voices are heard and identified so that the content provider can adequately respond.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, I would like the Ministry to elaborate on these operating procedures, such that creative work is protected and both content providers and complainers can openly dialogue and find common ground in a transparent way.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Deputy Speaker, I believe we all acknowledge the importance of positive engagement between the Government and the public.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Constant open dialogue between stakeholders help to ensure accountability and transparency as well as to encourage mediation and negotiation.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: This entails that a clear procedure of appeal be set in place.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: As this will be under the purview of the new IMDA, I would like to seek clarification from the Ministry on this process of appeal so that content providers have ample time to respond and negotiate.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: To take a recent example, the case in point was Newsha Tavakolian's exhibition "I Know Why the Rebel Sings" presented under the open programme of the Singapore International Festival of Arts.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: And is it turned out, such missed opportunities for engagement and dialogue ended in media furore and subsequent unhappiness, both of which could have been avoided.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Given that creative work would undoubtedly illicit subjective responses, I believe that the clarity of the procedures of negotiation and appeal would go a long way in preventing such situations and I urge the Ministry to relook the procedures as part of shaping the roles and responsibilities of the new IMDA.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Deputy Speaker, as a nation, we are encountering new sets of challenges and opportunities with media convergence.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: IMDA is well-placed to spur the development of our infocomm and media industries so that Singapore can continue to be a media hub and creative city.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, as IMDA focuses on its regulatory functions, I believe it is also essential for the newly merged entity to ensure that the space for creativity is not stifled.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It would, hence, be important for the Ministry to clarify how it aims to do both regulation and promotion as well as provide a transparent, accountable procedure where regulations and appeals are concerned.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Page: 121 One of the key factors then that led to the appointment of the panel was the increasing speed of how previously distinct media platforms were being merged and how the merger of these platforms was changing the way that content was being distributed and consumed.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Take, for example, the latest mobile app, Pokemon Go!, that has taken the world by storm and was launched recently in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am sure many Members here have their own encounters in their constituencies, of groups of people coming together almost in a zombie-like daze; and even some Members here might have evolved into pretty good Pokemon hunters themselves.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Pokemon Go's augmented reality engine allows players to interact with in-game characters based on their geographical location in real time, which further blurs the line between digital content and real life.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Or should we encourage and support our homegrown mobile app developers to tap on augmented reality technology to create the next Pokemon Go! even as we are aware of the potential issues that such apps might cause?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: From an ontological perspective, having a regulator which is also supposed to encourage the flourishing and development of what it regulates is inherently contradictory.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, how can IMDA ensure that it will play these dual roles impartially?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am sure that the regulation department would be a separate entity from the department that looks after the creative development of infocomm and media.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, how can we ensure that there will be no self-censorship from the creative department when they would or could be subconsciously toeing the line set by their regulation colleagues?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I think these are important details that IMDA needs to flesh out.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Having spent a substantial amount of my career in the media and education industries, I am of the opinion that the best way to foster creative infocomm and media industry development is to ensure a pipeline of high-calibre talent supply.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As the agency now responsible for developing the infocomm and media landscape of Singapore, it is thus paramount that IMDA has a comprehensive roadmap in place to attract and develop talent.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The notion of college dropouts who go on to create successful multi-million-dollar Internet companies might seem like a cliche but, in truth, there are many such stories.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Likewise, there are also many infocomm and media professionals who have succeeded with a diploma, and Page: 122 not a degree.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Teaching and training talent are as important as attracting talent to enter the industry and I believe that we need to ensure that our schools and training providers recruit good educators from the field to train the next generation of infocomm and media professionals.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although our post-secondary educational institutions, or PSEIs, are increasingly working closely with industry experts to bring their knowledge to the classrooms, they continue to use academic qualifications as one of the primary employment criteria for lecturers and educators.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As mentioned earlier, the infocomm and media industries reward talent based on abilities and skills, and not academic qualifications.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, using academic qualifications as a key evaluation tool to decide on whether a particular talent would be employed, and which scheme or career track they would enter into is counter to what is valued by these industries.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While many Ministries and Government agencies have combined their two tracks, I believe that this has yet to be the case in some of our PSEIs in terms of hiring educators.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This hiring right will boost the quality and training and education of infocomm and media students, which will, in turn, help strengthen the output in the infocomm and media industries.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With that, Sir, I conclude my speech in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, firstly, let me declare my interests as a Board Member of MDA.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: I also run the Asian business of a multinational media company, FremantleMedia.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This Bill and related amendments will be crucial in the evolution of our media landscape and our collective Smart Nation ambitions.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: It is also an opportune time to relook and enhance the functions and powers of IMDA to better suit the converged media landscape of today and the future and review the areas where we are found wanting.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Page: 123 Firstly, as a regulator, IMDA will have to contend with a plethora of new media entities, some existing but many that are still on drawing boards and others that do not yet exist.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This will require IMDA to have the capability to react and regulate with increased speed and efficiency.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: In January this year, global online content giant Netflix launched in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: As an aspiring Smart Nation and arguably one of the world's most connected cities, it was important to attract online leaders like Netflix, not just to launch their service here, but also to set up their Asian base on our shores.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: With Netflix, the biggest issue facing regulators all across Asia has been the issue of censorship.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Netflix's biggest attractions are its critically-acclaimed original productions.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Titles like "Orange is the New Black", "Narco" and "Marco Polo" are meant for mature audiences; and under local censorship guidelines, would be restricted to Restricted 21 (R21), or audiences over 21 years of age.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Some of our neighbours like Indonesia and Vietnam had initially banned Netflix from operating in their territories and would only issue an operating licence if their censorship fears are allayed.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: In my view, MDA's stand on Netflix should be commended.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The on-demand universe is very much a "lean forward" as opposed to a "lean back" experience, where much of the responsibility and choice lie solely with the consumer.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: More platforms like Netflix will be hitting our shores before we know it.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The likes of Amazon have already launched in many markets across the globe.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: IMDA will be faced with these imminent launches and similar pragmatic approaches would be needed.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Another more recent example is the Pokemon Go! game, which my colleague Darryl David alluded to.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: I think most of us in this House are familiar with this interactive augmented reality game that has taken Singapore and the rest of the world by storm.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: While personally I have yet to try the game – for fear that I would get addicted to it – in my household, the game is a hit not just with my 16-year-old son but with my wife, who has never been a fan of any game, virtual or physical.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: From a regulatory standpoint, again, MDA has approached the phenomenon in a calibrated, prudent manner.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Despite the initial furore in some quarters predicting that the game would be banned by authorities because of safety concerns, the game was launched with advice from the Police on personal safety and issues like trespass.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This is not any different from the approach taken in most countries or even the alerts built in within the game itself.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Again, and increasingly, consumers have to accept responsibility for playing the game.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The reality is that more games like Pokemon Go! will be coming on stream, and much of the responsibility has to fall on the consumers and not the regulators like MDA.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: I, for one, have already seen positives from the latest Pokemon craze.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Over the last couple of weeks, I have never seen as many people gathering together or walking around playgrounds, parks Page: 124 and shopping malls.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The game has made people get out of their homes, interact with others, particularly when they are exchanging tips on where and how to catch a Snorlax or Exeggutor ‒ forgive me, I do not know what it is, my wife put it there ‒ and it is clearly contributing to a healthier, outdoor lifestyle which can only be good for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: These examples clearly illustrate that IMDA has to be equipped and prepared to deal with these issues in a fast and expedient manner.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: However, Sir, there are also areas where I feel IMDA can take a more proactive role.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: One example is the recent issue over the securing of television broadcast rights for the Olympics that are currently being held in Rio.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: I am sure most of us in this House have been cheering on our Team Singapore athletes, such as Feng Tian Wei in table tennis, Quah Zheng Wen and Joseph Schooling in swimming, or Jasmine Ser in shooting, just to name a few.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: For those of us who watched the race, seeing a Singaporean from our tiny nation take on and beat the world's best brought about such great pride and joy and unity in spirit as Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: These are emotions you cannot put a value to.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This is not just about sport at the highest level.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This is about bringing people together, building national pride and identity among both sport and non-sport fans.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Now, imagine what would have happened if we were deprived of watching this "live".

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Many of us watched Joseph's dad, Colin Schooling's emotional interview right after watching his son win the Olympic Gold on "live" TV.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: As did hundreds of thousands of Singaporeans all across the island, the raw pride and joy were heard and felt across the island, not just among Singaporeans, but by many others, too, who live and work in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: So, why were we just hours away from not having access to a "live" telecast in a country that positions itself to the world as a modern, connected city, a "Smart Nation"?

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: High content costs were cited as the main reason. "It's a commercial decision", some said.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: As someone who works in the industry and who has had the experience of being both a buyer and a seller of such content and rights, I would like to very politely disagree with the reasoning put out, and the manner and approach to securing the 2016 Rio Olympics television rights.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Content costs, particularly sports rights, are expensive and have been for a while now.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This is a global trend, and one that is not unique to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: But the Rio Olympics, or any Olympics for that matter, carry a significance beyond a commercial price point.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Its value lies in that cloud of pride and joy that still hovers over the island.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: We felt it in this House even yesterday.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This is a sense of unity and spirit of invincibility of superhero proportions – that you can do anything if you work hard enough and persevere; that you could be the only person in the world to outswim your childhood hero and the most bemedalled Olympian in history.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Why else do we really spend Page: 125 millions on world-class sporting facilities?

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Why bother funding sporting associations, sportsmen and sportswomen?

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Why do we hire the best coaches and sporting administrators in the world?

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: If we say that we support Team Singapore and that we have built world-class facilities in support of our sporting dream, does this not extend to creating access to their moment of reckoning and glory for Singaporeans to support and celebrate?

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore broadcasters have spent hundreds of millions of dollars so that we can watch Manchester United on TV, week-in, week-out.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The rights to watch the Rio Olympics was a miniscule fraction of that amount for Singapore's fathers, mothers, brothers and sisters to watch their family members – the nation's best sportsmen and women on the world stage.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Perhaps, we can learn from our immediate neighbour, Malaysia, and how they approached securing the rights for the Olympics.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Radio Televisyen Malaysia, Malaysia's national free-to-air broadcaster; ASTRO, Malaysia's biggest cable broadcaster; and Telekom Malaysia – not just a telco but they also run an Internet platform – all came together to create a TV pool.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Each of these parties paid an equal one-third share of the costs.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: I am told that even with the split, it would be difficult for them to recoup their investment.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: But it was done in the spirit of national interest and they secured the rights in good time to be able to publish schedules in advance, as well as sell sponsorship and airtime around the Olympics to help recoup part of the cost.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: But after what happened with the TV rights for the Rio Olympics in Singapore, it is obvious that this cannot be left to chance.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: It is the very least the Government can do to honour the years of sacrifices made by our national sportsmen and women and their families.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The Olympics will certainly generate far more ratings and viewership numbers than most of our current PSB programmes.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: And, more importantly, create a sense of unity and national pride that is not tangible, and these values more than qualify as being of public service.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The next summer Olympic Games in 2020 will be held in Tokyo, in four years' time.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: With Tokyo just an hour ahead of us, most of the events will be telecast during our prime time, making it even more accessible to a bigger audience in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Having witnessed the impact of the Rio Olympics on Singaporeans of all walks of life, I would urge IMDA to secure these rights as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: There is also the contestable funding initiative that is open to all platforms in Singapore, as long as they make available their content to the public for free.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: In a recent dialogue session with independent producers, some of the feedback centred on inconsistencies in commissioning policies, particularly with cable operator StarHub.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: There have Page: 126 also been calls from the industry for several years now, asking for more transparency with regard to the quantum and projects.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: There is much expectation that with the establishment of IMDA, the agency can now finally make public, projects that are commissioned under the PSB framework, as well as the contestable fund initiative.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This should include details like genres, durations and production budgets.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This is a move in the right direction and will create more transparency and trust between broadcasters and production entities and build a more balanced and robust competitive environment that can only be good for the marketplace.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: It will definitely put paid to nagging rumours about broadcasters and their perceived favouring of inhouse producers vis-a-vis independent production entities.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: With more players entering the market because of digital platforms, transparency and openness are essential to creating more quality content and a more market-friendly Government positioning.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This brings me to my final point on the high-value freelance community in the media industry, and the role IMDA can play to regulate and foster growth.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The media manpower sector has an extremely large pool of freelance talents.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: There are thousands of freelances employed in the media sector with most companies employing them, as many of our SMEs are not capable of carrying big overheads.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: These talents span the gamut of the media sector, from film and video, broadcasting, publishing, online media to games.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Beyond supporting local platforms, the freelance community is also very involved in big-scale regional and global productions, such as Amazing Race Asia and Masterchef Asia, as well as several feature films.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: We expect to see this pool grow as many of the new generation of media practitioners prefer to work on their own schedules on a project-by-project basis.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: MDA and the Workforce Development Agency (WDA) have made much progress in working with the freelance community.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: I am heartened to hear that a few of my colleagues in this House have been working tirelessly with the freelance community, as well as agencies like MDA, WDA and the NTUC to find viable solutions.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore is too small, in my view, to have separate bodies representing writers, producers or camera crew.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: These have all been the bane of the freelance community for many years now, and IMDA has to urgently help find solutions.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Resolution of these issues would also help Singapore as a regional and global production hub, as international productions need a vibrant and quality freelance community to help support their projects.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: However, it is also an opportune time to relook and address some of the issues that have been around for a while now, as I have stated in my speech.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am particularly keen on IMDA's mandate to strengthen safeguards for consumers, highlighted in clause 61, as ordinary users are exposed to greater risks with the increasing use of infocomm platforms.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I recall 15 years ago, when Animal Concerns Research and Education Society (ACRES) was first started, we bought a 56-kilobit dial-up modem and struggled to get connected to the Internet.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Little did I anticipate that 15 years later, I can use a smartphone to take high definition videos and, within seconds, send it to anyone anywhere in the world.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, it is an understatement that the Internet has transformed our lives for the better.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, technology is a double-edged sword and I hope that while the agency promotes the use of the Internet and e-commerce, it can be accompanied by an equal measure of education on the risks they present.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It should inform consumers on the rise in phishing and malware attacks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For many Singaporeans, they may fall prey to this tactic.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have heard many stories from my residents who have been misled by fraudsters to share sensitive personal data or unwittingly clicked on links which downloaded malware.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: With the pervasive use of data, I welcome efforts to continue promoting and regulating data protection through PDPC.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will the Minister step up outreach efforts to the public and provide details on the methods it will employ?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, some of the functions of the agency include facilitating an adequate range of media services that serve the interest of the general public, ensuring that media services are provided at a high standard in all respects, particularly in respect of the quality, balance and range of subject matter of their content and ensuring that the content of media services is not against public interest, public order or national harmony, and does not offend against good taste or decency.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In essence, the authority will decide on behalf of the public, amongst others, the range, quality and content of media services.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Today, IDA and MDA are both regulators and developers of the infocomm and media sectors respectively, and we have found that this approach works well and allows us to achieve an appropriate balance between development and regulation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We do in fact have a process in place for appointing diverse representatives from the industry, so that their perspectives are incorporated into decisions, while at the same time being mindful of potential conflicts of interest.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: A good example is Mr Ganesh Rajaram himself who is from the private sector sitting on the MDA Board.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So we remain open to the representatives that we will seek to sit on our boards so that our boards can be dynamic and timely in terms of their response.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad has asked for further elaboration and examples of how IMDA will develop the infocomm media industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IDA and MDA are already working together to look into possible initiatives that will build on IDA's and MDA's strengths and will benefit the infocomm media industry as a whole.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Darryl David asked about our approach to Pokemon Go! and other cutting-edge mobile apps.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I think we would be quite circumspect about expanding IMDA's regulatory ambit without being clear about our real concerns, and whether there are other levers to manage these disamenities or undesirable outcomes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, the advisory from the Police is about the right response at this point in time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We must be mindful about not unnecessarily dampening the spirit of innovation that is so critical to the development of innovative products and services in this sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The integration of IDA Labs, the Games Solution Centre and Creators' Space that I mentioned in my earlier speech is precisely intended to help develop exciting new ideas, such as the next Pokemon Go!.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There are many more projects in the pipeline.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IDA's iSPRINT is today a very successful programme that helps SMEs raise their productivity through investments in infocomm.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We can extend iSPRINT to the media SMEs to help them use infocomm technologies to raise productivity and grow faster.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will share more details of these efforts in the coming months.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Moving forward, IMDA will also look into ways to support freelancers better, including the Member's suggestion of setting up a freelancers' guild.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Besides developing talent, amidst changing media consumption habits, we must continue to have good quality local programmes for Singaporeans to enjoy, build strong capabilities in the production of these local content, and develop effective channels that stay relevant.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA will continue to encourage this through PSB.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: PSB funds do not just fund Mediacorp programmes, but Page: 129 also support the growth of the independent media sector through outsourcing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Ganesh Rajaram commented on the importance of transparency in PSB funding.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We conduct regular audits of PSB funding expenditure to ensure that the funding agreements are adhered to, and that proper processes and internal controls are in place.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The PSB Contestable Fund Scheme, which was mentioned by Mr Ganesh Rajaram, is also open to all local production companies to enable the commissioning and development of innovative content with public service value.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad asked how IMDA will encourage infocomm media professionals to develop their skills and competencies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Through TeSA, which is an initiative under SkillsFuture, we can better plan, coordinate and enable the development of ICT professionals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have made it a point to partner major employers for TeSA, because employers must buy into our efforts to build a strong Singaporean Core.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There has been considerable progress since my announcement of TeSA in April this year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IDA has also been engaging key industry players at the senior management level and they have expressed strong support for TeSA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Besides TeSA, IMDA will also launch several exciting projects to nurture a generation of digital natives in time to come.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For example, the existing ICT Learning Roadmap will be augmented to include key media domains, such as storytelling, into an Infocomm Media Learning Roadmap.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This roadmap will encourage Singaporeans to develop skills that are valuable in today's digital age.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA will also be developing the Media Skills Framework for key job roles, which include current and emerging skills maps that indicate competencies for each occupational level and career progression pathways.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This will help to encourage employers to hire talent based on skills and competencies, rather than academic qualifications.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: On this point, I thank Mr Darryl David for his suggestion to look into harmonising degree and non-degree employment practices for infocomm media professionals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will work closely with the relevant agencies, such as MOM and MOE, as was suggested.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: These principles still remain relevant in a rapidly changing media landscape.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA will continue to regulate content, while ensuring that guidelines are in line with community values and social norms.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The relevant regulatory provisions will be found in subject-specific legislation, such as the Broadcasting Act, the Films Act, the Undesirable Publications Act and the Public Entertainments and Meetings Act.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I wish to assure Mr Kok that IMDA will continue to take seriously its role in promoting creativity and content creation, as has been done by MDA thus far.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As a content regulator, MDA Page: 130 will take into account community values before deciding on the classification, in order to strike a balance between the artistic merits of the performance and broader social norms.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In so doing, IMDA will be as transparent as possible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For the Les Miserables example raised, I have already given my written response to the Nominated Member Mr Kok Heng Leun's Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In short, MDA reviewed the feedback and established that the organiser had failed to inform MDA of a particular scene that had an impact on the classification rating.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This was conveyed to the organiser, who decided to remove the scene on its own volition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MDA also strives to inform organisers of its decision early, once all the supporting information and materials are received and processed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In a small number of cases, more time may be needed to assess the content due to its sensitive or controversial nature.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: MDA then conveyed clearly to the organiser that Singapore takes a firm stand against extremism and would not allow photographs that undermine public order or national interest or security to be displayed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Louis Ng shared his concerns on the protection of personal data.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We recognise that many companies collect and hold personal data, and it is important that they put in place measures to protect their customers' personal data.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: PDPC has undertaken many outreach activities to promote awareness of personal data protection in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: PDPC has also released a number of advisory guidelines, such as on securing personal data on electronic medium, so that companies have practical tips and resources to help them adopt better ICT security measures.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Moving ahead, PDPC will update their existing guidelines and also issue new guidelines and resources to help our companies, so that they can put in place better measures to protect their customers' personal data.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Louis Ng also raised an important point about instances of Singaporeans falling prey to phishing and malware attacks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Raising awareness of cybersecurity and heightening Singaporeans' vigilance against online cybercrime is something that all of us have to work together to achieve.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA will play a role as part of its outreach efforts, alongside partners, such as the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore, schools, and our law enforcement agencies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I agree that the parties should aim to conclude their negotiations early, especially given the significant interest by our public.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: However, we cannot compel parties to reach a deal that does not make commercial sense, or which results in escalating content prices in the long run.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And I take Mr Ganesh Rajaram's point that content prices will go up because it is in demand.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) and MCI will continue to monitor the content market developments closely.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Page: 131 Sir, I mentioned in my earlier speech that IMDA will encourage greater sectoral innovation and transformation through leveraging infocomm media technologies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Logistics is one such industry that can greatly benefit from this effort.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA, together with SPRING Singapore, has started to explore ways to leverage technology to help streamline delivery schedules, thus reducing truck congestion at loading bays of retail malls and increasing the productivity of logistics service providers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is currently being deployed at Tampines Mall, and initial results have been encouraging.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA is also working with the Housing and Development Board to deploy federated parcel lockers in residential areas, to make it more convenient for consumers to receive their packages, and to improve productivity for last-mile delivery services.
